Katie Hobbs is the Democratic incumbent running in a midterm under a Republican president, which historically favours the out-party. Polling I know of through mid-2026 showed her with a modest lead over the likely Republican nominees, and she had a strong fundraising advantage. Arizona remains a closely divided state that Trump won in 2024, so a Republican win is quite plausible. I have no reliable information on the actual November result, so this is a pre-election estimate.

Probability: 0.73

Jalen Duren was a restricted free agent with Detroit in summer 2026, coming off a breakout season, so the Pistons would be expected to match any offer sheet or re-sign him. By early September most free-agency movement is done, and I have no knowledge of a deal sending him to the Clippers. The Clippers were also not an obvious suitor with the cap room to force Detroit's hand. A sign-and-trade or later trade to Los Angeles before the October close is possible but unlikely.

Probability: 0.02

As of late September, the Dodgers, back-to-back champions in 2024 and 2025, are very likely in the playoff field and among the title favorites, though I can't confirm the final 2026 standings or seeding. Even the strongest team entering a 12-team postseason typically has only about a 15–22% chance of winning it all, given the randomness of short series. Their deep roster and recent October record put them near the top of that range, but uncertainty about a first-round bye and pitching health keeps the estimate from going higher. I estimate roughly 19%.

Probability: 0.19

I can't look up current prices, so this rests on my recollection that Brent spiked well above $100 in spring 2026 on the Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption, with the futures curve steeply backwardated toward the low-to-mid $80s for later months. I don't know where Brent traded on August 20, and the 84.99 strike is probably one of several Kalshi strikes set near the prevailing price. By August 31 the front-month contract rolls to a later delivery month, which in a backwardated market pulls the reference price down somewhat. With the price likely near the strike and no clear directional edge, I put this slightly below even odds.

Probability: 0.42

The market's exact definition isn't something I can confirm, but "blue tsunami" most likely requires more than a simple Democratic sweep, such as winning both chambers with large margins. As of mid-2026, Democrats were strong favourites for the House, but winning the Senate needed a net gain of about four seats on a difficult map, which markets put at roughly 35–45%. A tsunami-level threshold on top of that would be considerably less likely. I don't know the actual election results, so this is a prior-based estimate rather than a read of the outcome.

Probability: 0.1

I can't verify that price, but it is plausible and consistent with what I knew: Hobbs as a modest favourite in a Democratic-leaning midterm environment. A liquid market two months before the election is a meaningful signal, and it likely reflects post-primary polling I don't have, so I'm moving most of the way toward it. I'm stopping slightly short because Arizona is still a closely divided state and election markets at that range can overstate favourites.

Probability: 0.78

Missouri voters approved abortion rights by only about 52–48 in 2024, and the 2026 measure has fairly favorable ballot wording that bundles the repeal with popular items such as parental consent, rape and incest exceptions, and a ban on gender transition care for minors. Against that, abortion-restricting measures have lost even in red states (Kansas and Kentucky in 2022), and a midterm under a Republican president should favor the "No" side in turnout and fundraising. I have no reliable result or late polling to draw on, so this is an estimate from those fundamentals rather than from the outcome. On balance I see it as slightly more likely to fail than pass.

Probability: 0.4

A market price of 25% is real information I didn't have, and it's plausible for a two-time defending champion that is the betting favorite heading into October, so I'm moving most of the way toward it. I'm stopping slightly short because I can't verify the figure, and Manifold prices on popular favorites tend to run a little high compared to sportsbook-implied odds once the vig is removed. Even the best team in a 12-team playoff field rarely justifies much more than 20–25%, given how random short series are. That puts my updated estimate at about 23%.

Probability: 0.23

A live market price is much better information than my recollection, since I had no view of where Brent actually traded on August 20 and traders did. I can't verify the 60% figure, but taking it as stated, it implies Brent was sitting modestly above the 84.99 strike with about eleven days to go. I'm moving most of the way to it, holding back slightly because the figure is unverified and because the contract roll in a backwardated market is a small downward pull that the market may or may not have fully priced.

Probability: 0.57

I can't verify that price, but if the market was trading at 29% on 2026-10-09, that is better evidence than my guess, which rested on not knowing the market's exact definition. A 29% price suggests the threshold is closer to a Democratic sweep of both chambers than the more extreme bar I assumed, and it is roughly consistent with the 35–45% Senate odds I recalled from mid-2026. I still don't know the election results, so I'm moving most of the way to the market price, shading slightly lower because I can't confirm it and long-shot YES contracts tend to trade a little rich.

Probability: 0.26

I can't verify that price, but if the market really was at 16% on that date, that is real information and worth updating on: it suggests there was some rumor or reported Clippers interest that I'm not aware of.

I'd still stay below the market, for three reasons:

- **Thin markets:** Multi-outcome "next team" markets on Kalshi are often thinly traded, with stale last-trade prices and wide spreads, so 16% may overstate the true consensus.
- **Longshot bias:** Specific-team outcomes in these markets tend to be overpriced relative to how often they hit.
- **Structural barrier:** Detroit held matching rights on a restricted free agent coming off a breakout season, and a move would have had to be completed by October 21.

Weighing my prior against the reported price, I'd move up to roughly 8%.

Probability: 0.08

The Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem has resisted proof for decades, and the base rate for a Millennium Problem being resolved and widely accepted within any given year is very low. The market's wording ("the proof is probably valid") hints that a specific claimed proof may be circulating, but I'm not aware of one that has gained broad acceptance among mathematicians. Even a credible claim, such as the computer-assisted blow-up work by Gómez-Serrano's group with DeepMind, would likely need longer than the time remaining to be verified and widely agreed on. I therefore put the chance of a YES resolution by June 2027 at a few percent.

Probability: 0.04

Brenna Bird is the Republican incumbent in a state Trump carried by about 13 points in 2024, which makes her the favorite. However, she won only narrowly in 2022 (about 2 points, against a long-time Democratic incumbent), and 2026 is a midterm under a Republican president, with Iowa Democrats overperforming in 2025 special elections. I have no knowledge of the actual result, since my information ends before the November 3 election, so this is a forecast rather than a report. Weighing the state's Republican lean against the Democratic-leaning environment, I put Bird at roughly a 70% favorite.

Probability: 0.7

I could not look up the Kalshi market, so I am assuming the "combo" refers to two Senate candidates Joe Manchin endorsed, most plausibly Susan Collins in Maine and independent Dan Osborn in Nebraska. On that reading, Collins looked like a modest underdog (roughly 40%) and Osborn a clearer underdog against Ricketts (roughly 25%) as of my information through mid-2026. Both winning requires two underdog results that are not strongly positively correlated, since one is a Republican and the other an independent running against a Republican. That puts the joint probability at around 10%, with extra uncertainty because I am guessing at which two races the market covers.

Probability: 0.1

Without a live quote, I am relying on my recollection that Brent spiked above $100 during the 2026 Strait of Hormuz disruption and then eased back, with later-dated contracts trading lower than spot. A strike of 107.99 is most likely in the upper part of the range Kalshi lists for this monthly market, so the price on September 23 is probably below it. With only a week left, a move above that level would need a fresh supply shock. I put the chance at low but not negligible, given how volatile the market has been this year.

Probability: 0.12

I can't look up the BTC price as of September 3, 2026, so this rests on my recollection that BTC fell from around $90k in January 2026 to the $60–75k range through the first half of the year. If it is still near $70k, reaching $85,000 would need a rally of roughly 20% within a month, which historically happens less than about 10% of the time. If it has recovered to around $80k, the chance of touching $85,000 at some point in the month rises to roughly a third. Weighting those scenarios, with more weight on the lower price range, gives a modest probability.

Probability: 0.13

Mateus Simões took over as governor when Zema stepped down to run for president, so he has incumbency and the state machine behind him. But in the polls I know of (through mid-2026), he trailed well behind Senator Cleitinho, who led comfortably, and he also faced competition from names like Rodrigo Pacheco and Alexandre Kalil. His path requires either Cleitinho not running or fading, plus consolidating the right-wing vote to reach and win a runoff. I have no information on the actual result, so this is a forecast from pre-election polling, and I put his chances at low but not negligible.

Probability: 0.14

A 14% market price is real information, and it suggests traders see a more credible specific claim than I assumed, so I'm moving up. I'm not going all the way to the market, though, because Manifold long-shot markets tend to sit above the true odds: tying up capital to bet NO on a long-dated question is unattractive, so overpricing persists. The bar is also high, since even a serious claimed proof or blow-up construction usually takes more than a year of verification before mathematicians widely agree it is valid. Weighing the market against that base rate, I land at about 9%.

Probability: 0.09

A 63% market price is a reasonable piece of evidence, and I can't verify it, but it is plausible and not far from my own estimate. Markets aggregate polling and local information I don't have, so I weight it heavily, though my prior on Iowa's Republican lean and Bird's incumbency keeps me a touch above it. I still have no knowledge of the actual result, so this remains a forecast, now moved down from 0.70 to about 0.65.

Probability: 0.65

VA-11 is a Fairfax County–based seat that is safely Democratic; James Walkinshaw won the September 2025 special election with roughly 75% of the vote. Even if Virginia's mid-decade redistricting changed the lines, the proposed map was drawn to favour Democrats, so the seat should remain Democratic-leaning under either map. The 2026 national environment also looks favourable to Democrats, leaving only a small tail risk from an unusual upset or resolution quirk. I have no knowledge of the actual result, so this rests on those fundamentals.

Probability: 0.985

The framework was only signed on June 26, 2026, and Israel has already told Lebanon that leaving the pilot zones "will take time," which points to slippage past an end-of-August window. Past Israeli withdrawals in southern Lebanon have tended to be delayed or left partial, as with the 2025 deadline extension and the five retained points. Hezbollah's explicit rejection adds a risk of incidents that would give Israel reason to pause, and resolution likely requires deployment in both zones, including the harder one north of the Litani. On the other hand, strong US pressure and the pilot's small scale make a quick, symbolic handover plausible, so I put this at roughly one in five; I have no reliable information on how events actually unfolded after the agreement.

Probability: 0.2

I can't verify that 43% figure, but if it is accurate it is strong evidence, because a live market price reflects BTC's actual level on September 3, which I don't know. A 43% price on a "touch $85,000 this month" contract would imply BTC was trading around $80k, not the $70k I leaned toward. My earlier estimate rested on a weak guess about the price, so I'm updating most of the way toward the market. I'm stopping somewhat short of 43% because I can't confirm the quote.

Probability: 0.36

I have no reliable data on the 2026 standings as of early September, so this estimate rests on priors rather than the actual standings. Colorado went 43-119 in 2025 and entered 2026 as the preseason favourite for the worst record, at roughly 40–50%. Other plausible contenders such as the White Sox, Nationals, Angels, Cardinals and Twins split the remainder. Without knowing where Colorado stood with a month left, I stay near the preseason figure, shaded slightly down for uncertainty.

Probability: 0.4

The 2026 WNBA season is 44 games, so 30 wins requires roughly a .682 pace, about what the Aces managed in 2025 when they went 30-14 and won the title. I don't have reliable data on their 2026 record as of early September, so I can't tell whether they are on pace. Preseason win lines for a defending champion would likely have sat around 28-29, making 30+ somewhat less likely than not. Without the current standings, I'm leaning on that prior and putting it modestly below even.

Probability: 0.3

Ronaldo Caiado is running as the PSD candidate, but as of my last information polls had him in the mid-single digits, far behind Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, who dominate the first-round field. To win he would need to overtake Flávio for the right-wing runoff spot and then beat Lula, and nothing I know of suggests that consolidation was happening. I don't know the actual result, so this is a forecast from the polling picture rather than a reported outcome. A long-shot path remains if the Bolsonaro candidacy collapses, so I put it slightly above zero.

Probability: 0.02

Serbia's recent parliamentary turnouts were about 58.6% (2022) and 58.8% (2023), but the student-led protest movement has mobilised voters heavily, so a turnout in the low-to-mid 60s is plausible if an early election is held. The bloated voter roll (many registered voters live abroad) makes turnout much above 66% hard to reach, which keeps 62-66% as one of the more likely ranges. However, I can't confirm that an election has actually been called for 2026 — the regular deadline is 2027 — and if none is held in the market's window this range likely resolves NO. Weighing roughly a one-in-three chance of this range given an election against the timing uncertainty, I land a little under a quarter.

Probability: 0.23

A 39% market price is real evidence, if accurate (I can't verify it), since traders may be pricing in reporting on withdrawal logistics that I don't have, so I'm moving up rather than holding at 0.2. I'm not going all the way to it, though: thin geopolitical markets often run high on deal-implementation questions shortly after a signing, and the structural obstacles haven't changed. Israel has already signalled delay, Hezbollah rejects the framework, and resolution likely requires deployment in both zones within about seven weeks. Weighting the market at roughly half against my own estimate puts me at about 0.29.

Probability: 0.29

Several Cabinet members have already left in 2026 by my recollection, including Kristi Noem being removed as DHS Secretary in March, and Pam Bondi and Lori Chavez-DeRemer departing in April. Since a departure has already occurred, the "no one leaves" outcome should be effectively ruled out. The only residual uncertainty is how the market's rules define a qualifying departure, which I could not check here.

Probability: 0.01

I can't verify that price, but if the market really was at 56% on September 3, that is strong evidence: late in the season it reflects the Aces' actual record and remaining schedule, which I don't know. My earlier 0.3 was only a preseason-style prior, so it should give way to a live market that has most of the season's results priced in. I'm moving most of the way to the market, with a small discount because I'm taking the quote on your word and thin late-season markets can be noisy.

Probability: 0.53

SC-07 (Myrtle Beach/Pee Dee area) is a solidly Republican district that Trump carried by roughly 20 points, and it has been held comfortably by Republican Russell Fry. Even in a strongly Democratic midterm environment, a district this red would be very unlikely to flip. I have no information indicating an unusual candidate problem or upset in this race. The small remaining uncertainty reflects only tail risks, since I can't confirm the actual result.

Probability: 0.98

I can't verify that price, but if the market was trading at 33% on that date, it is real evidence and worth weighting, since traders would have known whether an election had been called, which was my main source of doubt. My own estimate was already about one in three conditional on an election being held in the window; the discount came from timing uncertainty, which a 33% price suggests the market did not consider large. I still wouldn't move all the way to the market, because multi-bucket Polymarket ranges often sum to more than 100% and thinly traded ones can be stale. So I'm moving most of the way toward it, not matching it.

Probability: 0.3

Burnham was not an MP for most of 2026, so he needed to win a by-election and then a Labour leadership contest before being sworn in by 31 October. My recollection, which I can't verify, is that after Labour's poor May 2026 elections a route opened for him via a Makerfield by-election in June, with Starmer under heavy pressure to go. If he won that seat and a contest is under way, he would be the favourite and a result by the autumn conference is plausible. But the by-election outcome, the contest timetable and rival candidates are all uncertain to me, so I put this near even.

Probability: 0.5

The Washington Post report describes military action in Mali as only under consideration, with senior U.S. officials disagreeing on whether to proceed, and Mali's government had received no official contact as of late July. Moving from deliberation to an actual strike within a single month is uncommon, especially in a new theater without established basing or host-nation coordination. That said, this administration has shown willingness to strike quickly in new countries (e.g., Nigeria in late 2025), so the chance is not negligible. I have no knowledge of the actual outcome, so this rests on base rates and the reported state of deliberations.

Probability: 0.06

I have no data on August 2026 yields, so I can't confirm whether the 30-year has already closed below 5% this month. The question's framing suggests yields were above 5% when it was written, and the Yahoo article describes a sustained run above that level rather than a brief test. However, a YES needs every August close at or above 5%, and a single dip on a soft data print or a rally in bonds would resolve it NO. With the buffer above 5% unknown and 11 days left, I put this somewhat below even.

Probability: 0.4

The Pitt won Drama Series in 2025 for its first season, and its second season (January–April 2026) is eligible for the September 14, 2026 ceremony with strong reception. Several of last year's main rivals, such as Severance and The White Lotus, are not eligible this cycle, which leaves Pluribus as the most credible challenger. Returning winners with sustained acclaim usually repeat, and I recall The Pitt being the heavy favourite, though I have not checked the current market price. I put the chance of a repeat win at about 85%, allowing for a Pluribus upset.

Probability: 0.85

I can't verify that 74% figure, but if it's accurate it deserves real weight: my 0.5 came from shaky recall of the by-election and contest timeline, whereas market traders on 23 July would have known whether Burnham had won his seat and what the leadership timetable was. A price that high suggests he was already an MP and the clear favourite in a contest due to finish before the deadline. I'd still shade slightly below the market, since prediction markets of this kind can run hot on a front-runner and any slip in the timetable past 31 October resolves NO. So I'm moving most of the way towards it, not all the way.

Probability: 0.7

Digger is Alejandro G. Iñárritu's Tom Cruise film, due for release on 2 October 2026, so the score will be settled by reviews landing just before the question closes. Iñárritu's record on Rotten Tomatoes, as I recall it, is uneven: Birdman (91) and Amores Perros (93) cleared 85, but The Revenant (78), 21 Grams (80), Babel (69), Biutiful (66) and Bardo (59) did not. I have no review data for Digger itself, so this rests on that base rate of roughly two in seven, with a divisive auteur comedy being a plausible candidate for the 70s–80s range. Tom Cruise and a major awards-season push add some upside, but not enough to move far from the base rate.

Probability: 0.27

A 31% market price is real evidence if accurate, since traders may be weighing signals I lack, such as reporting on force movements or the administration's leanings; I can't verify the figure, though. Still, thin markets on dramatic geopolitical events tend to overprice action, and the price likely reflects the Washington Post story's salience more than new information. The underlying facts remain that officials were divided, Mali had received no official contact, and the window is only one month. I'm moving up meaningfully to weigh the market, but not all the way to it.

Probability: 0.13

I can't verify that 60% figure, but if it's accurate it is real information: forecasters on Aug 20 could see the actual yield path, which I can't. A 60% price implies the 30-year had not yet closed below 5% in August, which removes the main scenario behind my lower estimate. It also implies the cushion above 5% was modest, since a comfortable margin with only seven trading days left would price well above 60%. I'm moving most of the way toward the market, keeping a small discount because the figure is unverified.

Probability: 0.56

I can't verify that price, and it conflicts with what I recall: Kristi Noem was removed as DHS Secretary in March 2026, and Pam Bondi and Lori Chavez-DeRemer left in April 2026. If those departures count under the market's rules, "no one leaves" is already dead, and a 99% YES price would make little sense. Even for a later-created market covering only remaining members, 99% would be oddly high with nearly three months and a post-midterm period still to go. I've raised my estimate slightly for the chance the market is defined in a way I'm not anticipating, but I'm not moving to the figure you quote without seeing the market's rules.

Probability: 0.04

Carlson's statement was a vague pledge to "help build" a third party, with no named organization, timeline, or staff announced. Standing up a party committee and filing FEC Form 1 within roughly five weeks of today's date in the question (by end of August 2026) would be unusually fast. The closest precedent, Elon Musk's "America Party" announcement in July 2025, did not, as far as I recall, produce a genuine FEC filing by Musk in a comparable window. The main residual risk is a quick or loosely attributed filing being counted, which I judge small.

Probability: 0.02

Renan Santos, the MBL founder running for Partido Missão, was polling in the low single digits in the data I know of, far behind both Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, who looked set to take the top two spots. For him to finish second, one of those two would have to collapse or leave the race and he would also have to overtake every other right-of-centre candidate. I have no result data for the October 4 first round, so this rests on pre-election polling alone. That makes a second-place finish a very remote outcome.

Probability: 0.01

Minnesota's 4th district is centered on St. Paul and is safely Democratic (roughly D+17), held by Betty McCollum of the Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party (Minnesota's Democratic affiliate) since 2001 with consistently large margins. Nothing I know of suggests a competitive race in 2026, and the national environment in a midterm under a Republican president favors Democrats further. The only residual risk is a resolution technicality around the DFL label, which Polymarket normally treats as Democratic.

Probability: 0.99

Connecticut is a reliably Democratic state, and incumbent Governor Ned Lamont is seeking a third term with strong approval ratings. The 2026 midterm takes place under a Republican president, which historically favors Democrats. Republican challengers (such as Ryan Fazio or Erin Stewart) face a steep climb, and no Republican has won the governorship there since 2006. I have no knowledge of the actual result, so this is a forecast, with a small allowance for an upset.

Probability: 0.96

MT-01 is a Republican-leaning district (Zinke won by about 3 points in 2022 and about 7 in 2024, with Trump carrying it by roughly 11), so a Democrat needs a sizeable swing. Working from memory rather than current polling, Zinke's retirement makes this an open seat, and a midterm under a Republican president should favour Democrats. That combination puts the race in competitive territory, but the district's partisan lean still makes the Republican the favourite. I put the Democrat's chances at just under one in three.

Probability: 0.3

Digger is Alejandro G. Iñárritu's Tom Cruise comedy, due out October 2, 2026, and I have no review data for it yet, so this rests on base rates. Iñárritu's Rotten Tomatoes record is mixed: Birdman (91) and Amores Perros (93) clear the bar, but 21 Grams (80), The Revenant (78), Babel (69), Biutiful (66) and Bardo (59) do not. Anticipation and the Cruise pairing suggest a strong reception is plausible, but his divisive, ambitious style makes a score strictly above 80 slightly less likely than not. I put it a little under even odds.

Probability: 0.42

Iran has denied IAEA access to Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan continuously since the June 2025 strikes, and it publicly rejected Vance's June 2026 claim that inspections had been agreed. Even if a peace deal were reached soon, negotiating inspection modalities and safely entering bombed sites would likely take longer than the under-two-month window remaining. Iran's past pattern has been to use inspector access as leverage and to restrict rather than expand it under military pressure. A rapid breakthrough is possible but unlikely.

Probability: 0.04

Alaska's August top-four primary and the November ranked-choice general fall after my knowledge cutoff, so I don't know the result and am estimating from the pre-primary picture. Bernadette Wilson was among the strongest Republicans in a crowded field on fundraising and early polling, and Republicans are generally favoured statewide in Alaska. Against that, the field included other credible Republicans such as Nancy Dahlstrom, and a Democrat such as Tom Begich could be competitive in a Democratic-leaning midterm year under ranked-choice voting. I put her as the single most likely winner but below even odds.

Probability: 0.4

Federação União Progressista (União Brasil + PP) combined won about 106 seats in 2022 against PL's 99, so it is a genuine contender on incumbents, mayors and campaign funding. However, PL likely benefits from presidential coattails with a Bolsonaro-family candidacy, and my recollection is that it gained deputies in the 2026 party-switching window while União Brasil lost some. The PT-led federation is a third, less likely contender for the largest bloc. Working from memory rather than current polling or seat projections, I put PL as favourite and UPB as the main alternative.

Probability: 0.27

The Landtag has 71 base seats with 36 constituencies, and recent polling as I recall it puts AfD at roughly 37–40%, which translates to about 29–32 proportional seats depending on whether BSW and the Greens clear the 5% threshold. AfD could also win around 28–33 direct mandates, and since overhang seats are compensated by enlarging the parliament, its seat total is effectively the higher of the two figures. That puts the central estimate right around the boundary between the 28–31 and 32–35 brackets, with some chance of 36 or more if AfD outperforms. I have no result data for this election, so this is a forecast from polling and the electoral system rather than a known outcome.

Probability: 0.4

Helder Barbalho is term-limited, and his vice-governor Hana Ghassan (MDB) is running with the backing of the state's dominant political machine, which makes her the favourite. Éder Mauro (PL) is the Bolsonaro-aligned name and polled competitively in early surveys, but I recall reports he might run for Senate instead, and Ananindeua mayor Daniel Santos could split the opposition vote. This is from memory rather than current polling, so I can't confirm his candidacy or his standing a month before the first round. Overall I treat him as a clear underdog with a real but small chance, most plausibly through a runoff.

Probability: 0.1

I can't verify that 32% figure, but if it's accurate it deserves some weight, since a market may reflect news about the talks that I don't have. Still, the fundamentals point strongly the other way: Iran publicly denied agreeing to inspections, it has blocked access to these three sites for over a year, and even a signed deal would need time to arrange safe entry into bombed facilities before September 1. Markets on dramatic geopolitical breakthroughs with short deadlines also tend to overprice YES. I'm moving up modestly to reflect the market signal, but not close to 32%.

Probability: 0.09

I can't verify that price, but if the market was at 4% on October 9, that is after the August primary and would reflect information I don't have — most likely that Wilson either failed to advance to the top four or was trailing badly in general-election polling. My earlier 0.4 rested only on the pre-primary picture, so a post-primary market price should outweigh it almost entirely. I'm leaving a small margin above 4% for the chance the quoted price is wrong or stale.

Probability: 0.05

Under the old map (I recall the Virginia Supreme Court striking down the 2026 mid-decade redistricting amendment, though I can't verify this), VA-01 remains a Trump +5 seat held by Republican incumbent Rob Wittman, who won by about 13 points in 2024. A Democratic-leaning national environment of roughly D+6 would put the district's baseline near even, with Wittman's incumbency tilting it slightly Republican. Democrats have a credible challenger and the seat is likely rated Lean Republican, so this is a competitive race but not a coin flip. I put the Democratic chance a bit under even.

Probability: 0.4

A market price of 45% is meaningful evidence if accurate, though I can't verify it, and it is higher than I would have expected given PL's likely coattail advantage. Markets on this kind of question aggregate seat projections and post-window bench sizes that I only recall imperfectly, so I should move a good way toward it. I don't move all the way, because the figure is unconfirmed and thinly traded markets with several outcomes can be mispriced. I also have no knowledge of the actual election result, so this remains a forecast rather than a report.

Probability: 0.38

A market price is real information, and my 0.40 was a rough estimate built from district fundamentals rather than from polling, so it deserves some weight. I can't verify the 47% figure, but if it's accurate it suggests traders saw the race as closer to a true toss-up than I did, possibly reflecting district polling or fundraising that I don't have. I'm not moving all the way to it, because an incumbent who won by 13 points in 2024 still seems to me a slight favourite in a seat Trump carried by about 5. So I'm moving most of the way toward the market, not adopting it outright.

Probability: 0.45

Ohio's 2026 Senate special election pits Jon Husted (R) against Sherrod Brown (D), and I don't have the actual result, so this is a forecast from what I know of the race through mid-2026. Polling showed a close contest, with Husted leading by low single digits in some surveys and Brown tied or slightly ahead in others. Brown lost by only about 3.6 points in 2024 even as Trump carried Ohio by 11, and 2026 looked like a more Democratic-leaning midterm environment. Husted was a modest favourite to win, but clearing a 4-point margin requires him to outperform most polling, which I put at roughly one in four.

Probability: 0.27

Virginia's mid-decade redistricting amendment was, as I recall, struck down by the state Supreme Court in May 2026, so VA-05 should be running on its old lines, which Trump carried by roughly 12 points and McGuire won by about 15 in 2024.
